thread:
Elaine: Quick question — when we say 'happy path' for the hosting abstraction, do we mean the end-to-end case where requests never hit the private-side adapter? Or do we include fast fallbacks like KV cache reads that can route locally?
Devon: I think the 'happy path' should be defined by latency SLOs more than by topology. If it meets the latency/cost profile, it's happy.
Elaine: Good point. The confusion comes up for autoscaling decisions: hosted wants to prefer pooling on shared nodes, private wants local affinity.
Alex: Practically speaking we have three orthogonal axes: latency SLO, data residency (private vs shared), and cost budget. The adapter interface should expose signals for all three.
Sree: +1. Also we need to be explicit about what each adapter promises: e.g., 'serve-prefix-from-kv' vs 'fallback-to-remote'. Right now the adapter manifest only says capabilities: [kv-cache, streaming, quantized], but not semantics.
Elaine: Can we sketch a tiny manifest extension? Something like:
```
capabilities: {
  kv_cache: {mode: local|remote|hybrid, stale_ttl_ms: int},
  routing: {priority: int, allowed_fallbacks: [variant-id]},
}
```
Devon: That would help. Also add an explicit 'latency_budget_ms' hint so orchestrator can pick routing (hosted vs private) by budget.
TJ: Be careful: hints are advisory only. If a customer pins model variant in private, we must respect residency even if it breaks latency SLOs. Need clear precedence rules.
Elaine: Right — precedence: customer pin > residency policy > latency_hint > cost_hint. Let's note that in the doc.
Alex: What about probe-first semantics? For example, if hosted can't satisfy kv cache miss quickly, we probe private path and use it only if it meets the budget. Probe needs a failure budget too or we'll cascade.
Sree: We implemented probe-first in the runtime before, but it created load spikes on private pools because probes happen synchronously. Suggestion: continuous health scoring + cheap async probe + sticky fallback for X minutes.
Devon: Also we should add an escape hatch: a policy flag `prefer_stable_affinity` that disables aggressive probes and enforces stability for dedicated/private deployments. Useful for enterprise customers who want predictable tail latency.
Elaine: Ops question: how does telemetry reflect when a request touches multiple adapters (e.g., hosted -> fallback -> private)? We currently only log final model. We need full path traces.
TJ: Agreed. Add a `routing_trace` field in the request-level span with steps and latencies. Minimal example: `["hosted:5ms","kv-local:1ms","private-fallback:30ms"]`.
Alex: For implementation, adapters should return a small enum for result: OK_HIT, OK_FALLBACK, ERR_TIMEOUT, ERR_AUTH. Keep it compact for high QPS.
Sree: For the SDK surface, we should not leak internal names. Offer a `route_metadata` object but sanitized. Internal fields can be in debug logs only.
Elaine: Next steps? Sounds like we need a short RFC: define manifest extension, precedence table, probe semantics, routing_trace spec, and a couple unit tests (probe spike guard, precedence enforcement).
Devon: I'll draft the RFC and include an example matrix mapping customer policy -> routing decision for common cases (hosted-only, dedicated-resident, private-pinned).
TJ: I'll add a security note about KMS/HSM boundaries when falling back to private — must never ship unencrypted prompt to hosted if customer requires local crypto.
Elaine: Good catch. Add that to the precedence table as well.
Sree: Can we also add a tiny integration test harness that simulates latency distributions and validates routing decisions? I can wire something into the runtime tests.
Elaine: Perfect. Who owns the RFC? Devon?
Devon: Yep, assigned to me. Will drop a PR by EOD tomorrow.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://go/repo/pulls/4021 — draft title: "Routing semantics: happy-path, probes, and adapter manifest extensions" :sparkles:
Elaine: Thanks — I'll review and add the precedence matrix comments.
Alex: I'll sketch the telemetry trace format and a small option for ingest-level sampling.
Devon: Thanks all. Putting follow-ups in the RFC. :thumbsup:
